segments.t: At home on their day off, Max cooks an omelette to win Vika back after she gives him the silent treatment, right before Kostya drops off his toddler son Styopa for the morning.
Но хуже всего, когда вас игнорируют.
Не стоит злиться друг на друга.
Let's walk through each Russian line and see how Max and Kostya phrase things.
'It is always nice when people love you.' Russian uses an impersonal third-person plural verb without a subject pronoun to express a general truth like 'people love you'.
Но хуже всего, когда вас игнорируют.
'But worst of all is when they ignore you.' The comparative form for 'worse' combines with the genitive pronoun for 'all' to build the superlative phrase 'worst of all'.
'Hi, I made an omelette for you.' The masculine past-tense ending on the verb shows that a male speaker completed the action of cooking.
Не стоит злиться друг на друга.
'There is no point getting angry at each other.' The reciprocal expression at the end literally repeats the word for 'friend' with a preposition to mean 'at one another'.
'We are family, after all.' Russian drops the present-tense verb 'are', and the little emphatic particle in the middle adds the warm sense of 'after all'.
'Well, and what does that mean?' Conversational particles at the start soften the question before the demonstrative pronoun and present-tense verb.
'Have you forgiven me?' The feminine past-tense ending '-a' on the verb shows that Max is addressing a woman.
'We quarrel over such little things.' The reflexive verb ending marks a mutual action done together by both partners.
'Soon we will have a baby.' Instead of 'to have', Russian often says a child 'will appear' by us using the preposition for 'by' plus the genitive pronoun.
'You have a day off today, right?' The noun for 'day off' comes from the word for 'exit', literally a day when you go out rather than to work.
'I slept so well.' The prefix and reflexive ending on the verb mean not just sleeping, but getting a full, refreshing night of rest.

'Sit with Styopa for a bit.' In Russian, 'to babysit' is expressed simply as sitting with someone for a while, using the instrumental case after 'with'. Now listen to the full exchange again at natural speed.
Но хуже всего, когда вас игнорируют.
Не стоит злиться друг на друга.
When you watch the opening scene, listen for how Russian says 'we are family' in just three short words without any verb for 'to be'. See you in the next scene.

lines.fragment: Но хуже всего, когда вас просто игнорируют
не стоит злиться друг на друга
